To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. The first modest signal of HIV vaccine efficacy from the RV 144 clinical trial in Thailand, and the recent advances in understanding the structure of the HIV envelope glycoproteins, have led to new directions for HIV vaccine development; 2. The HIV reservoir has proven very difficult to eliminate, but the prospect of achieving a classic cure is now a realistic scientific goal; 3. Strategies that control viral rebound after ART discontinuation offer the prospect of a functional cure.
• The RV 144 trial demonstrated the first signal of vaccine efficacy against HIV infection, and the RV 144 regimen is a useful starting point for future trials

1) HIV vaccine research is making significant advances in both the RV 144 follow on studies and structure based immunogens that elicit broadly neutralising antibodies; and 2) Cure research is making significant progress with the potential of achieving a classic cure or a functional cure
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and development of novel, potent, orally available, small molecule, antiviral agents for the treatment of HIV/AIDS and other viral infections.
the development of new HIV vaccines, and the eradication of HIV infection.
the following questions: 1. How can we improve the efficacy of HIV vaccines? 2. How can we cure HIV infection?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the HIV epidemic is at an important crossroads and that the scientific community is now in a position to accelerate our response to the epidemic and to make significant progress toward ending the epidemic.
we have the science to end HIV/AIDS.
the HIV pandemic can be ended, and the end of the epidemic is in sight.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been able to show that the use of the HIV-1 vaccine candidate Ad5gag/pol/nef can be safe and immunogenic, and that the vaccine can be administered in a cost-effective manner.
we have been able to develop a new class of drugs that are highly potent, well-tolerated, and have a favorable resistance profile.
we have been able to identify and isolate broadly neutralizing antibodies from HIV infected people and use them to develop new vaccines.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HIV reservoir is not a single entity, but is a complex and dynamic collection of cells and viral forms that are present in different tissues and at different stages of latency.
HIV is a very complex virus and we have to use a combination of approaches to control the virus and to prevent it from spreading.
we can now see a path to an end to the HIV/AIDS pandemic and it will be based on the science of HIV vaccine and cure.
